articles.title: Deepika's 8-goal blitz powers India to 19-0 thrashing of Uzbekistan at Asian Games
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: India's women's hockey team began their Asian Games campaign in emphatic fashion, cruising to a 19-0 win over Uzbekistan in their opening Pool B match.
articles.body: India's women's hockey team began their Asian Games campaign in emphatic fashion, cruising to a 19-0 win over Uzbekistan in their opening Pool B match here on Sunday.The contest was expected to be heavily one-sided and India lived up to those expectations from the opening whistle, repeatedly breaching an Uzbekistan defence that struggled to cope with the intensity and quality of the Indian attacks.Deepika was the star of the show, scoring eight times in a remarkable individual performance. She found the net in the 8th, 22nd, 25th, 33rd, 36th, 38th, 41st and 54th minutes to lead India's goal fest.Lalremsiami opened the scoring in the seventh minute with a close-range field goal before Deepika added India's second a minute later. Ishika then extended the lead in the 11th minute with a superb first-time finish from the left side of the circle after being set up by Sunelita Toppo.Baljeet Kaur made it 4-0 in the 12th minute, while Neha added another field goal six minutes later.Deepika then took centre stage again, converting a penalty corner with a powerful dragflick into the bottom-right corner. Navneet Kaur followed with a field goal before Deepika struck once more from a penalty corner to send India into half-time with an 8-0 advantage.The onslaught continued after the break, with India adding 11 more goals across the final two quarters.Alongside Deepika's eight, Ishika scored three times, while Lalremsiami, Baljeet, Neha, Navneet Kaur, Lalthantluangi and Sakshi Rana also got on the scoresheet.Ishika struck in the 42nd and 54th minutes after her first-half goal, Navneet added another in the 45th, while Lalthantluangi scored in the 43rd and 51st minutes. Sakshi Rana also found the net in the 43rd minute.The gulf between the two teams was also reflected in the possession and attacking pressure, with Uzbekistan struggling to retain the ball for sustained periods.The match also marked a milestone for veteran India goalkeeper Savita Punia, who earned her 320th international cap. With that appearance, she joined Vandana Katariya as the joint-most capped Indian women's hockey player.Savita had little involvement in the contest, however, as Uzbekistan rarely managed to create meaningful pressure and spent much of the match trying to contain India's relentless attacks.India, the second-highest-ranked side in the competition, will next face Indonesia on Monday.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: China's 13-year-old swimmer Yu Zidi clocks 2:05.08 to break Asian Games record, wins 200m butterfly gold; she also became youngest medallist in World Championships swimming history in 2025
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: China's teenage swimming sensation Yu Zidi completed a memorable Asian Games debut by winning the women's 200m butterfly gold with a new Games record .
articles.body: China's teenage swimming sensation Yu Zidi completed a memorable Asian Games debut by winning the women's 200m butterfly gold with a new Games record in Japan on Sunday.The 13-year-old, who turns 14 next month, clocked 2:05.08 to break the Asian Games record set by China's Zhang Yufei at the Hangzhou Games three years ago. Zhang had won the event in 2:05.57, and Yu finished nearly half a second quicker.Yu crossed the finish line 3.36 seconds ahead of fellow Chinese swimmer Chang Mohan, who took silver.The victory gave Yu her first major individual gold medal and came in the first of the three individual events she is scheduled to compete in at the Asian Games, where the swimming competitiona are being held in Tokyo.Youngest medallist in World Championships swimming historyYu announced herself on the world stage last year when she became the youngest medallist in World Championships swimming history. At the age of 12, she won bronze as part of China's 4x200m freestyle relay team.She also finished fourth in three individual events at the World Championships, narrowly missing out on medals.This year, Yu has continued her rise, including a win over American Olympic champion Regan Smith in March.The schoolgirl, known for her pixie haircut, is expected to be among the contenders at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.Despite her success, Yu has spoken about the pressure that comes with competing at such a young age.Ahead of last year's China National Games, she said the pressure of trying to win the 400m individual medley almost became too much.Her coach encouraged her to keep going and "believe in yourself", she said, as quoted by AFP.Yu went on to win four medals at the National Games.Her rapid rise has also sparked discussion within swimming over the mental and physical demands of elite-level training and competition at such a young age.Under World Aquatics rules, the minimum age for international championships is 14, although exceptions can be made for younger swimmers if they meet the qualifying standard.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Ebbw Vale beat Wizards in perfect start to SRC
articles.summary: Ebbw Vale, Newport and Cardiff extend winning starts to the 2026-27 Super Rygbi Cymru campaign.
articles.body:
Ebbw Vale are setting the pace in Super Rygbi Cymru (SRC) after a 52-26 win at Aberavon.

The Steelmen, runners-up in 2025-26, earned a second six-point haul on the bounce when running in eight tries at the Talbot Athletic Ground.

The Wizards led 19-12 at half-time thanks to two tries by wing Frankie Jones after Gavin Parry's opener.

Dragons Harry Rees-Weldon and fellow wing Dafydd Thomas scored in the first half for Ebbw and six more tries followed after the break.

Hookers Ieuan Morris and James Talamai, full-back Morgan Rees (2), Thomas and centre Ethan Phillips all scored, while flanker Rhys Thomas earned the Wizards a four-try bonus point.

Newport are also two wins from two after beating champions Llandovery 46-26 at Church Bank.

The Drovers, who lost their opening fixture at Pontypool, started the better as number eight Daniel Gemine crossed for the opener.

But the visitors dominated the remainder of the half as scrum-half Dafydd Buckland grabbed two tries and wing Oli Andrew, lock Ethan Phillips and flanker Hunter Ward touched down.

Fly-half Ioan Hughes added to Gemine's try for Llandovery in the first half, and they continued their fightback to get the four-try bonus thanks to scores by wing Aaron Warren and replacement back Joshua Thomas.

Newport sealed a comfortable victory - and earned an extra bonus point - thanks to tries by flanker Tiehl Chatham and centre Brogan Leary.

Cardiff are the third team to have won twice after a 49-35 win against Swansea at the Arms Park.

Back-row forward Tirion Bowen, hooker Tom Howe and lock Tom Cottle scored for Cardiff in the first half, but Swansea led 23-21 thanks to wing Brandon Wood's double and a try by centre Jack Hoskins.

Wood completed his hat-trick to stretch the Whites' lead, but Cardiff responded impressively through prop Ioan Emanuel, full-back Isaac Marsh, centre Jason Harries and wing Dewi Cross.

Cardiff were denied an extra bonus point by fly-half Josh Phillips' late try.

Bridgend held off a spirited Pontypool comeback for a 50-38 away win.

The Ravens stormed to a 31-7 lead inside 25 minutes as wing Ben Evans, flanker Tom Jevons, wing McCauley Rowley (2) and centre Ryan Wilkins all crossed, with centre Ryan Conbeer adding a sixth first-half try for the visitors.

Pontypool clawed the score back to 43-38 thanks to tries by locks Liam Antrobus and Dan Hill, flanker Scott Matthews, scrum-half Ellis Lewis, fly-half Evan Lloyd, wing Rhys Cole, but Rowley completed his hat-trick to secure the victory.

Rygbi Gogledd Cymru (RGC) claimed their first win of the season by beating Carmarthen Quins 36-29 in Colwyn Bay.

Prop Pedr Jones, full-back Dion Jones, centre Danny Cross, wing Sam Jones, hooker Osian Burt scored tries for RGC, while Quins left with a pair of bonus points thanks to a penalty with the last kick by Madoc Evans.

articles.title: 76ers 3 goals: Labaron Philon Jr. needs to bring offense to bench unit
articles.summary: Philadelphia 76ers rookie Labaron Philon Jr. needs to bring offense to a bench unit that will need to support the starters.
articles.body:
In this new series, Sixers Wire looks at the 16 players, per Spotrac , that comprise the Philadelphia 76ers roster — 14 under standard contracts and the two players on two-way deals — and gives each three goals for the 2026-27 season.

The new season begins on Oct. 20, and training camp is right around the corner. Now is the time to begin previewing the new season of adventure that is Sixers basketball.

Up next in this series is rookie guard Labaron Philon Jr., the No. 22 pick of the 2026 draft. The young guard from Alabama averaged 22.0 points, 5.0 assists, and 3.5 rebounds while shooting 39.9% from deep as a sophomore for the Crimson Tide and will be looking to bring that scoring productivity to the league.

For Philon, his three goals are as follows:

The Sixers will have other scorers off the bench to rely on ( Anfernee Simons , for one), but if Philon is to really establish himself in the league, then he will need to find a rhythm early and often. He had his ups and downs in the summer league out in Las Vegas, but the dynamic guard showed off some real potential. He has an ability to really get into the paint, draw defenders, find different ways to finish at the basket up and around defenders, and is able to knock down tough shots. He needs to find that rhythm with the Sixers quickly in order to catch the eye of coach Nick Nurse for rotation minutes.

If there is one real question with Philon, it's his 3-point shot. He saw a big improvement in college, as he went from 31.5% from deep as a freshman on 3.4 attempts per night up to 39.9% on 6.2 attempts as a sophomore, before then shooting just 25.8% on 7.8 attempts in the summer league. He has a smooth shot and has a maniacal work ethic, which will serve him well next to Tyrese Maxey and VJ Edgecombe , and that will help him improve along the way. If Philon can come in and knock down 3s at a 34-to-37% clip, then it would be a big help for Philadelphia 's bench unit. He can be a microwave scorer for the Sixers in the long run.

Heading into the 2026 draft, Philon was expected to be a lottery pick. He then tumbled all the way to No. 22 to Philadelphia as it was obvious that there are some teams that have questions about his game. He can prove those teams wrong by bringing that offensive ability to the league right away. If Philon can knock down shots at a consistent rate, get to the basket, and make plays for others right off the bat, then he will be a helpful player right now. If he can become a defensive pest in the future, then he will immediately become a consistent rotation player. He should carry a chip on his shoulder heading into his maiden season.
